title: The BB84 Protocol
description: Bennett and Brassard 1984: bases, sifting, error detection, and eavesdropping

questions.question: The BB84 protocol was first published in 1984 by
options: Charles Bennett and Gilles Brassard
Artur Ekert and Charles Bennett
Peter Shor and Charles Bennett
Charles Bennett and Peter Shor
questions.correctAnswer: Charles Bennett and Gilles Brassard

questions.question: BB84 is a protocol for
options: distributing a shared secret key using quantum states sent over a quantum channel
sending a message directly with unbreakable confidentiality
computing large prime numbers faster than any classical algorithm
producing a tamper-proof digital signature
questions.correctAnswer: distributing a shared secret key using quantum states sent over a quantum channel

questions.question: In BB84, Alice encodes each random bit using one of four polarisation states. Which set does she use?
options: the rectilinear basis ($0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$) and the diagonal basis ($45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$)
the rectilinear basis only, at $0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$
any four mutually orthogonal states of her own choosing
the left and right circular polarisation states only
questions.correctAnswer: the rectilinear basis ($0^\circ$ and $90^\circ$) and the diagonal basis ($45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$)

questions.question: How many mutually unbiased measurement bases does BB84 use?
options: Two: the rectilinear basis and the diagonal basis
Four, one for each of the four polarisation angles
Three, including a circular-polarisation basis
One, which keeps the encoding as simple as possible
questions.correctAnswer: Two: the rectilinear basis and the diagonal basis

questions.question: For each bit, Alice must choose
options: a random basis and then a random state within that basis
a random state, with the basis fixed by a public schedule
a fixed basis, with the state chosen at random
whichever basis minimises the eavesdropping risk
questions.correctAnswer: a random basis and then a random state within that basis

questions.question: Bob measures each arriving photon using
options: a basis chosen randomly and independently of Alice's choice
the same basis Alice used, which he deduces from the photon itself
a basis chosen after he reads Alice's transmission record
the basis that maximises his chance of a matching outcome
questions.correctAnswer: a basis chosen randomly and independently of Alice's choice

questions.question: During the sifting step, Alice and Bob publicly compare
options: which basis each of them used for each photon
the measured polarisation angle of every photon
the numerical value of every random bit
the intensity of every transmitted photon
questions.correctAnswer: which basis each of them used for each photon

questions.question: Photons for which Alice and Bob used different bases are
options: discarded, because their outcomes are uncorrelated
kept, because each still yields a valid random bit
retransmitted by Alice for a second attempt
used to probe the eavesdropper's presence
questions.correctAnswer: discarded, because their outcomes are uncorrelated

questions.question: To test for eavesdropping, Alice and Bob publicly compare
options: a sample of their sifted key bits, computing the fraction that disagree (the quantum bit error rate)
the total energy of the photons they received
the time taken for the photons to arrive
the number of photons their detectors registered
questions.correctAnswer: a sample of their sifted key bits, computing the fraction that disagree (the quantum bit error rate)

questions.question: In ideal single-photon BB84, if the quantum bit error rate exceeds roughly $11\%$, the correct response is to
options: abort the run, since the key bits can no longer be assumed secret
continue, since the error rate only affects how long the key is
continue and encrypt the remaining bits with a one-time pad
discard only the photons that were lost in the fibre
questions.correctAnswer: abort the run, since the key bits can no longer be assumed secret

questions.question: If Eve measures every photon in a random basis and resends it, her presence causes
options: an error rate of about $25\%$ among the sifted bits, far above the tolerable threshold
an error rate of about $11\%$, just at the tolerable threshold
no errors at all, because resending produces the original state
an error rate of $50\%$ in every run regardless of the basis choice
questions.correctAnswer: an error rate of about $25\%$ among the sifted bits, far above the tolerable threshold

questions.question: Eve cannot simply copy the transmitted photons and measure her copies later because
options: the no-cloning theorem forbids making a perfect copy of an unknown quantum state
photons travel too quickly to be copied by any device
she would need a full quantum computer to perform the copy
the channel destroys the states before any device could intercept them
questions.correctAnswer: the no-cloning theorem forbids making a perfect copy of an unknown quantum state

questions.question: Eve cannot measure the photons in a way that always reveals their basis, because
options: the four states are not mutually orthogonal, and a measurement that distinguishes non-orthogonal states inevitably disturbs them
she would need to know the output of Alice's random number generator
a photon is absorbed if she measures in the wrong basis
her own basis choice is correlated with Alice's basis choice
questions.correctAnswer: the four states are not mutually orthogonal, and a measurement that distinguishes non-orthogonal states inevitably disturbs them

questions.question: The central principle behind BB84's eavesdropping detection is
options: any attempt to gain information about a quantum state disturbs it, and the disturbance appears as errors in the shared key
photons cannot be stored for longer than a few nanoseconds
classical light cannot be amplified without adding noise
the key length always decreases when a photon is lost in the channel
questions.correctAnswer: any attempt to gain information about a quantum state disturbs it, and the disturbance appears as errors in the shared key

questions.question: Alice sends the state $|+\rangle$ and Bob measures in the $X$ basis. In BB84 language this means
options: the two used the same basis, so the bit is kept
the two used different bases, so the bit is discarded in sifting
an eavesdropper must have intercepted the photon
the bit is retained as a marker of an erasure event
questions.correctAnswer: the two used the same basis, so the bit is kept

questions.question: In BB84, Alice chooses the rectilinear basis and sends the $90^\circ$ state. With the convention $0^\circ = 0$ and $90^\circ = 1$, the bit encoded is
options: either $0$ or $1$ with equal probability until Bob measures
$\tfrac{1}{2}$, since a single photon carries half a bit

questions.question: After error checking, the surviving key is usually shortened by classical privacy amplification, which
options: hashes the remaining bits so that Eve's information about them is reduced to a negligible amount
repeats the transmission with more photons until the error rate falls
pads the key with random bits to hide its length
replaces the key with a fresh one-time pad of the same length
questions.correctAnswer: hashes the remaining bits so that Eve's information about them is reduced to a negligible amount

questions.question: For BB84 to be secure, the classical channel must be
options: authenticated, so that Eve cannot impersonate Alice or Bob during sifting
private, so that Eve cannot read the announced bases at all
encrypted with a pre-shared key
left unauthenticated, since the quantum channel already provides authentication
questions.correctAnswer: authenticated, so that Eve cannot impersonate Alice or Bob during sifting

questions.question: Why is it acceptable for Alice and Bob to announce their bases openly?
options: the basis announcements alone reveal no information about the sifted bits, and Eve's disturbances are caught by testing the key
the announcements are encrypted with a pre-shared key before transmission
only the bases are ever announced, never the bit values
the eavesdropper is assumed not to monitor classical channels
questions.correctAnswer: the basis announcements alone reveal no information about the sifted bits, and Eve's disturbances are caught by testing the key

questions.question: A practical implementation of BB84 must use single-photon or weak pulses, because
options: multi-photon pulses can be attacked by a photon-number-splitting attack
multi-photon pulses cannot be modulated fast enough for the key rate
single-photon states cannot be produced by any laser
weak pulses avoid the need for single-photon detectors
questions.correctAnswer: multi-photon pulses can be attacked by a photon-number-splitting attack

questions.question: The decoy-state method used in real BB84 systems is a technique to
options: defeat photon-number-splitting attacks by varying the intensity of the pulses
reduce the dark-count rate of the detectors
correct for polarisation drift in the fibre
measure the channel loss before sending any key data
questions.correctAnswer: defeat photon-number-splitting attacks by varying the intensity of the pulses

questions.question: In BB84 the sifted key consists of the photons that
options: were measured in the basis matching the one in which they were sent
were measured in any basis, with mismatched ones later corrected by Alice
were sent using a basis fixed by a public schedule
passed through a quantum repeater during transmission
questions.correctAnswer: were measured in the basis matching the one in which they were sent

questions.question: A key practical advantage of BB84 over entanglement-based protocols is that it
options: needs no entangled-photon source or pair distribution, only a prepare-and-measure setup
needs no single-photon source at all
works over longer distances without repeaters
needs no authenticated classical channel
questions.correctAnswer: needs no entangled-photon source or pair distribution, only a prepare-and-measure setup

questions.question: A key practical disadvantage of BB84 compared with post-quantum cryptography is that it
options: requires specialised quantum hardware and a dedicated optical link
cannot be used over existing optical fibre
produces keys only at very low rates on short links
requires the two parties to share a secret key in advance
questions.correctAnswer: requires specialised quantum hardware and a dedicated optical link

questions.question: BB84's security is described as
options: information-theoretic, resting on the laws of quantum physics rather than on computational hardness
computational, resting on the difficulty of a problem such as integer factoring
conditional, resting on the physical security of the laboratory
heuristic, supported only by experimental data
questions.correctAnswer: information-theoretic, resting on the laws of quantum physics rather than on computational hardness

questions.question: Why does BB84 use four states in total rather than just two?
options: two non-orthogonal bases are needed, so that no measurement can identify the basis without introducing detectable errors
four states give two bits of redundancy per transmitted photon
a qubit requires four basis values, since $|0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle$ are not enough
four states double the key rate achievable on a single channel
questions.correctAnswer: two non-orthogonal bases are needed, so that no measurement can identify the basis without introducing detectable errors

questions.question: Alice sends a photon in the state $|+\rangle$. Eve measures it in the $Z$ basis and resends the result. Bob then measures in the $X$ basis and obtains a value different from Alice's intent with probability
A deployed QKD system is best described as
options: a source of key material that must be combined with authenticated classical encryption
a complete replacement for all conventional encryption
a device that encrypts the user's data directly with single photons
a network protocol that removes the need for authentication
questions.correctAnswer: a source of key material that must be combined with authenticated classical encryption
